recipes.name: Slow Cooker Pork Chops and Sauerkraut

steps.text: Place pork chops in the slow cooker crock. Pour sauerkraut with juice over the top.
Cook on Low for 8 to 9 hours or High for 4 to 5 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Pork Chops and Sauerkraut
raw_recipe.description: Simple, straightforward and downright delicious, this slow-cooked pot of pork chops and sauerkraut hits the spot at the end of a chilly day.
raw_recipe.name: Slow Cooker Pork Chops and Sauerkraut

recipeInstructions.text: Place pork chops in the slow cooker crock. Pour sauerkraut with juice over the top.
Cook on Low for 8 to 9 hours or High for 4 to 5 hours.

review.reviewBody: This is a great basic one to start with when you don't have a lot on hand, I doctored it up with stuff I scrounged up in cabinets: started with 2 huge and frozen solid out of freezer bone in pork chops, coated each with onion soup mix, got can of sauerkraut, added a little mustard, threw on some caraway seeds, and put over pork chops. cut up a couple of apples and put on top, poured bottle of beer over it all and put on low for 8 hours, came out so tender and really yummy, we all loved it. Probably could have used just a littel more juice but no complaints. I find a lot of items are so tender but overcooked really in the slow cooker so I am away 10 hours or more. So find using frozen meats elimiated need to thaw and prevents the complete disintegration of the meat when you cut it. Was still extremely tender and bone just fell out - will definately make again!!

This recipe is awesome!! I looked at the reviews and tweeked it a little bit. I seasoned the pork chops with onion powder, garlic, pepper and soul seasoning. I seared them in one tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil in a skillet on top of the stove before putting them in the crock pot. Next, I layered sliced onion and sliced apple. I put the sauerkraut in a bowl and stirred in 1/4 cup of light brown sugar and 1/4 cup of apple cider vinegar for the last layer. I cooked it on high for 4 hours. The chops were so tender that they fell off of the bone and the sauerkraut was to die for! Mashed potatoes and green beans for sides. It was a big hit with my bunch and I will definitely be making this again!

This was amazing! My husband said it was by far the best thing I've made. I did sear the chops 5 min on each side and seasoned them with garlic salt, dried onion, and black pepper. Then I added 1/4 cup brown sugar to the sauerkraut along with a little more water. My chops were thin so I only had to cook them on low for around 4 hours. Thank you for sharing this recipe! Will definitely make this again!!

I did what other reviewers did, add stuff! I used some onion soup mix on the frozen chops, topped with the sauerkraut, sprinkled dry mustard, brown sugar, black pepper, and about a cup of white wine. Cooked on high for a bit then dropped back to low to finish. DH said "Put it on the list!". I will try this again with a pork shoulder or even chicken thighs! Yummy!

Me ALSO‼️ I added a cup of white Zinfandel, 16 ounces of sauerkraut from the jar like it said, a splash of bold horseradish mustard, about a little over half a cup of brown sugar (we like it sweet), and some chopped up red onion which lined the bottom. Tender and delicious!

It's a basic recipe that my grandmother taught me growing up. I added La Flor Adobo Con Sazon, and 2-3 Tbsp of Kikkoman Teriyaki/Marinade Sauce to give it a kick of flavor. I also added 3 Tbsp of water so that it wouldn't dry out. I used the low setting for 6 hours and it was falling apart. If you want variety, you can add green peppers and/or onions. This recipe is great if you don't have a lot of ingredients on hand.

My first time making Pork & Sauerkraut in the crockpot. I used “thin” cut chops(3). Seasoned chops with garlic 🧄 powder, onion 🧅 powder and “seared “ chops in margarine on Medium-High heat for 1 minute per side. Once chops and sauerkraut were in the crockpot, I added Pepper and Caraway Seed. After being on “LOW “ setting for 6 hours, the pork fell right off the bone 🦴. I did add some water 💧 due to not enough juice with the sauerkraut. I was pleasantly surprised how moist the chops were.👍. I definitely 💯 will be making this again in the future.

As written, this recipe is a good starting point. I spiced it up by following other reviewers suggestions. Sprinkled chops with salt, pepper, and garlic powder and seared for 2 minute per side in a hot skillet. Transferred chops to the slow cooker, poured 32 oz of sauerkraut (the hubs has a big appetite) on top, and sprinkled with 1/4 cup brown sugar and caraway seeds. The end result was absolutely delicious and it is such a simple recipe. Definitely a keeper!

this is the base of a recipe my polish landlady makes for me from time to time. she usually uses kielbasa type sausage rather than pork chops. I like the idea of the pork chops as it reduces the salt. here is how I revised this dish. I added half a cup of water, half a cup of low-sodium broth, cook bacon pieces with onion. I used a small pork loin, combine the sauerkraut bacon and onion water and broth over the roast and slow cooked in my hot pot. I did braised the roast on all sides in the bacon and onion drippings. turned out perfect and not too salty. Thanks for sharing.

Easy and delicious! I usually sear boneless pork chops first. I prefer a less sour sauerkraut so I like to rinse the sauerkraut then add 1/4 c (or so) of water with TBS (or so) of brown sugar, and some caraway seeds. The slow cooking really makes the pork, as well as the sauerkraut, so tender. A few slces of crumbled up cooked bacon also adds to the flavor (in case you have any leftover from breakfast )

1. browned chops and de-glazed with beer. 2. seasoned with salt and pepper 3. added one medium sized onion (sliced) 4. added 8 oz sliced mushrooms 5. added remaining beer (used New Castle dark beer) review: my husband said it was the best pork recipe we have cooked to date. He was ready to eat it all! The pork came out very tender and juicy. As for me, I don't like sauerkraut nor the smell of it - it definitely smelled like it throughout the house. I did taste the pork and it was good. We will be making this again, for him.
I seasoned the pork chops. Added red potatoes, (quartered.) Finger Carrots. Sliced apple.
I have made this quite a few times over the past 2 years. Today I added one medium sliced onion and 3 diced idaho potatoes. So incredibly delicious!
I made this but I put brown sugar and a Little apple in it. It is so good I add potatoes in the crockpot and it's. A one pot meal

Tried this for the first time and must say it is scrumptious! I did add touch of salt and black pepper on the pork chops before layering them (8) with two cans of sauerkraut. I did cook it on high but used a liner bag in my slow cooker so the chops weren't dried out and the sauerkraut was still juicy. Did do instant potatoes but plan to make au gratin potatoes next time.
No changes, fabulous flavor!! So simple that it hardly counts as cooking!
Tasty, but dry. May try to sear the chops next time before placing in slow cooker.
The pork chops were so tender. I added a can of potatoes.
Quick and easy and it tastes good.
